input.summary: Jordan Doe's identity was used from 198.51.100.23, a known-malicious bulletproof VPS (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING, NL; tagged k8s_api_bruteforce and open_docker_registry:5000). The real Jordan Doe is on PTO from 10-12 to 10-19 and normally uses macOS, but this client was kubectl on Linux. The same playbook ran on all three payments-prod clusters in sequence: AWS EKS 14:02-14:25, GCP GKE 14:38-15:01, Azure AKS 15:11-15:34. On each cluster the actor checked their own permissions, listed namespaces, failed to read kube-system secrets or create a kube-system job, then read the payments secrets and payments-db-credentials. Next they created a privileged pod, debug-tools-7f9c (hostPID, host / mounted, not on the allowlist), and exec'd nsenter into the node. From the node they took the cluster-admin argocd-application-controller service account token and used it from the same outside IP (that account should only run in-cluster) to create a cluster-admin ClusterRoleBinding, jdoe-break-glass, for jdoe. With that access they set up persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet kube-metrics-agent and a CronJob node-cert-rotate (every 15 minutes), both pulling images from the attacker's registry at 198.51.100.23:5000, and a NodePort service metrics-agent-np on port 30080. The alerting cluster-wide secret list was their last step on each cluster, so all secrets on all three clusters should be treated as exposed.

This is the standard 'kubectl debug node' pattern and she was otherwise doing routine reads. Benign, though it is not on the allowlist, so follow up on policy.
argocd-application-controller activity from its in-cluster IPs (10.0.12.108, 10.128.0.104, 10.224.0.102) is normal GitOps traffic. Only its use from 198.51.100.23 is malicious.
ClusterRoleBinding updates by eks:addon-manager, system:addon-manager and aksService at 03:05 come from control-plane IPs. These are routine addon reconciliation.
Many developers and SREs exec'd into app pods and read namespaced secrets from corporate egress 203.0.113.x with their usual clients. This is normal daily activity.
daemon-set-controller pod creates, node kubelet traffic, cluster-autoscaler, prometheus and coredns are all normal in-cluster system activity.
